title: Synthetic cohorts & cost-fingerprint: per-route observability for embeddings + rerank
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Ship route-aware observability primitives for the embeddings + reranking endpoint so PMs, SREs, and ML engineers can answer: (1) why did this route's latency/cost change, (2) is ranking quality degrading for a customer cohort, and (3) which optimization (batching, cache, quant) will reduce unit cost without harming rank quality. Deliverables: 1) per-route dashboard template with p50/p95/p99 decomposition for embed and rerank phases, KV cache hit heatmap, batch size distribution, and a cost fingerprint (model token cost + infra estimate); 2) tracing spans and attributes to tie latency to code hotpaths and kernel choices; 3) synthetic cohort runner to compute MRR/TopK drift over baseline and feed alerts; 4) alerting rules and runbook for regressions (latency and rank quality). Acceptance criteria: - Dashboard exists and is templated for any route_id with sane defaults. - Traces emitted for 95% sampled requests and aggregated counters for all requests. - Cost-fingerprint calculation correlates with billing to within 10% for test routes. - Synthetic cohort job runs daily and triggers sample alerts when MRR drops >5% relative to rolling baseline. - Runbook published and on-call escalation configured.

implementation_notes: Emit per-phase histograms (embed vs rerank) with explicit bucket boundaries to compute p50/p95/p99 without heavy aggregation work.
Add a lightweight cost estimator: cost = tokens_in * model_cost_per_token + tokens_out * model_cost_per_token + infra_est_per_second * observed_latency_seconds.
Synthetic cohort runner will replay a fixed prompt set and compute MRR@10 and NDCG weekly; store baselines per-route and per-cohort.
Sampling strategy: deterministic hash(route_id) % 100 < 5 for full trace capture; counters emitted for all requests with route_id label to maintain dashboard accuracy.
Alerting: two rule classes - (A) latency/cost spike auto-alert (p95 > 2x baseline for 10m) and (B) quality drift (MRR drop >5% vs 7-day baseline).
